newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end weaker, Santander slides.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end weaker, Santander slides.

text.p: Chilean shares closed softer in erratic trade on Thursday, with Banco Santander-Chile among the biggest losers after posting disappointing first-half results, traders said.

The bolsa is seen opening slightly firmer as the market looks to regain its footing in the wake of regional turmoil caused by instability in Brazilian equity markets, said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investment.
"The bolsa is searching for a new point of equilibrium. It's reasonable to think it will rise a little tomorrow," he said.
The 40-share index ended down 0.89 percent at 131.46 points. The general index lost 0.64 percent to 5,709.08 points on turnover of 11.3 billion pesos.
Traders said investors were waiting for first-half company results, many of which are to be published next week.
The banking sector's results, released Thursday, were mixed, with strong earnings from Banco Santiago STGa.SN, Banco BHIF and Banco de Chile, Tagle said.
Santander's profits were hit by costs from last year's merger, including a revision of Banco Osorno's loan portfolio which was not up to the the Spanish bank's standards, he said.
"The merger process has been most expensive than we imagined," Tagle said.
Santander reported that six-month net earnings rose to 12.47 billion pesos from 10.69 billion pesos last year. Its stock closed down 4.18 percent to 27-1/2.

Other decliners included forestry stocks, which slid amid concerns sparked by a California court ruling barring the U.S. government from issuing new import permits for Chilean logs and chips, traders said.
Compania de Petroleos de Chile SA, or Copec, lost 1.9 percent to 2,010 pesos, while Compania Manufacturera de Papeles y Cartones SA, or CMPC, shed 1.68 percent to 5,280 pesos.
